summary: China's youth jobless rate eased to 18% in September but is still the highest for that month since 2024, and Beijing set up a giant state company to manage the country's data for AI.
body: China's statistics bureau said on Wednesday that unemployment among 16-to-24-year-olds who are not in school fell to 18.0% in September, from 18.9% in August, as the effect of summer graduation faded [^1][^2]. That is still the highest September reading since the bureau began leaving students out of the count in January 2024 [^1]. For 25-to-29-year-olds the rate was 7.4%, and for 30-to-59-year-olds 3.9% [^1][^2]. Caixin reports that new jobs this year came mostly in software and IT and in tourism-linked work such as hotels, restaurants and transport [^1]. My read: for young graduates, finding a first job is still hard, even as overall growth holds up.

In technology, China launched the China National Data Group on Tuesday, a wholly state-owned company run by the central government and based in Xiong'an, a new city near Beijing [^3]. Its job is to develop and use the country's data, which Beijing has treated since 2020 as a basic input to the economy alongside land, labour and capital [^3]. It is backed by state telecom and power companies [^3], and it becomes the 100th company directly overseen by the central government, according to Chinese state media cited by Quartz [^4]. Data is the raw material AI models learn from, so the move fits China's push to build its own AI, but Caixin notes that questions about who owns data, privacy and how data is traded remain unsettled [^3].

reads.title: China creates National Data Group to advance data economy
reads.summary: Explains the new state data company and includes a useful timeline of how China came to treat data as an economic resource since 2020. Partly paywalled.
